how: We read the website of every Kansas City wedding florist listed on Lazo (138 listings, 112 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: grocery store floral counters, a produce market, delivery-only shops, a nonprofit that recycles event flowers, and venues and chapels listed under florists. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: What is grown locally in my month, and what has to be shipped in? Kansas City has flower farms within an hour, and summer heat is hard on some stems.
Do you design and install at the venue, or deliver arrangements? Installation, teardown and delivery are separate lines.
Can I see a full wedding at a budget like mine, including centerpieces and ceremony pieces, not just a bouquet?

picks.name: Love, Lilacs- Weddings + Events Florist
picks.blurb: Lexi of Love, Lilacs holds a degree in event management with a second minor in floral design, and the studio says it does not believe in copy-paste flower recipes. Every wedding design is custom, and the site calls her your behind-the-scenes bridal bestie.

picks.name: Wild Hill Flowers and Events
picks.blurb: A Kansas City wedding florist and planning firm in Spring Hill that designs for everything from a small, intimate gathering to a large formal event. Wild Hill's consultations start by identifying the elements that fit your style, then the team does the work.

picks.name: Blush and Blossoms Co.
picks.blurb: Mary Hagemeister founded Blush and Blossoms in 2018 after starting with flowers made in her kitchen for family and friends, then an in-home studio, then a rented space for clients. A luxury wedding florist in Kansas City who says she builds a relationship with every client she designs for.

picks.name: The Cottage Rose
picks.blurb: Ferrell approaches floristry through the lens of design, with a master's in architecture from the University of Kansas behind her sense of composition and proportion. The Cottage Rose makes modern, sculptural wedding florals and architectural installations in Kansas City.

picks.name: Belcher Event Services Team, LLC
picks.blurb: Custom wedding flowers and wedding planning from Kristin Belcher in Liberty, who learned floral design while running a Kansas City venue from 2021. BEST-KC also does prom flowers and weekly blooms, serving the Kansas City area.

picks.name: Beco Flowers
picks.blurb: Beco Flowers opened in the Crossroads Arts District in 1999, an urban flower boutique from owner Rebecca Ederer that specializes in weddings and events as well as everyday orders. The approach is simple, clean and organic, letting the flowers do the work.

picks.name: Flowers By Emily
picks.blurb: A Leawood floral boutique of more than 19 years that specializes in garden-style arrangements with lush color and texture, and a full menu for weddings and events. Flowers by Emily says you will not find generic catalog arrangements, and delivers across the KC metro.

picks.name: Pritzy Floral Design Studio
picks.blurb: Pritzy Floral was founded by Shahidah Salaam in 2014 with a focus on transforming weddings through bespoke floral design and decor, and has grown into a Grandview shop that also handles everyday delivery. Elegant blooms with intention, in its own words.

picks.name: Talk ta Me Floral
picks.blurb: A family-owned shop on Purple Meadows Lavender Farm in Spring Hill, serving Johnson County since 2016, with wedding arrangements alongside everyday delivery to Gardner, Olathe, Louisburg and nearby towns. Talk Ta Me also offers flower embossing for a printed message.

picks.name: BOOTSTRAP BLOOMS
picks.blurb: Janalynn Joy Walker of Bootstrap Blooms grew up in Topeka, graduated from Kansas State and lived around the country for 25 years before joining the wedding floral industry about four years ago. A wedding-focused floral business for couples west of the metro.

picks.name: Stonebriar Farm
picks.blurb: StoneBriar Farm is a family-owned wedding venue and flower farm in De Soto that sells seasonal, locally grown flowers to individuals and to florists, with sunset u-pick evenings. Worth knowing if you want local stems or want your florist to source from a farm.

picks.name: Flutter Farms
picks.blurb: Flutter Farms is a regenerative flower farm in Belton specializing in dried flowers, floral design and wedding florals that outlast the day. It also runs u-picks, workshops and a self-serve farmstand.
